svg.title: What /proc/PID/environ returns while a child process execs
svg.desc: A timeline of one exec. Right after a vfork-style spawn returns, a read can still see the parent's environment. After the new address space is mapped, a child of a non-dumpable process is unreadable until the exec marks it dumpable. The process then gets its new name, but its environment reads empty until the kernel fills in the environment pointers; only then does the read show the job marker.
svg.text: One exec, as a reader of /proc/PID/environ sees it
A right after a vfork-style spawn: the parent's environment (never seen directly)
B a child of a non-dumpable process: EACCES (5 of 2,000 probes)
C the new name comes first: empty for 0.018 ms (median), 0.139 ms (max)
Measured on Linux 7.0. The fix reads again on empty or denied, with pauses doubling from 1 ms.
